chunks: And Dāwūd al-Raqqī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Your breaking the fast in your brother's home is better than your fasting seventy times, or ninety times."

key_terms.أَخِيكَ: your brother, meaning a fellow believer

ai.seo_question: Is breaking a recommended fast to eat at a fellow believer’s home more virtuous than continuing the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the virtue of strengthening brotherly bonds through shared hospitality, even in the context of recommended fasting. It emphasizes that social harmony and honoring a fellow believer can outweigh repeated voluntary acts of fasting.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1797 - It is narrated by Dawud al-Raqqi from Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)), Imam (as) said:
"Breaking your fast at your brother's home is better than fasting seventy or even ninety times."
